title: Observability Gatekeeper and Latency Attenuation
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Objective:
Build an "observability gatekeeper" component and coordinated latency-attenuation workflow that ties tracing hook signals, metric/log pipeline enrichments, and dashboard-derived SLO state into more precise burn-rate and anomaly-driven paging decisions. The goal is to reduce noisy pages by 30% while improving mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for true degradations by surfacing higher-fidelity contextual signals to oncall.

Background:
We currently rely on simple SLI thresholds and ad-hoc metric alerts that cause frequent false positives during controlled background tasks (KV-rewrite, cache-warm, backup windows). Tracing hooks exist in multiple services but lack standardized enrichment and downstream propagation into the metrics/log pipeline. Dashboards show per-route P50/P95/P99 but are not programmatically queried for anomaly context before pages are generated.

Scope and goals (MVP):
- Create a lightweight gatekeeper service that consumes enriched trace markers and SLO status to compute a confidence score for paging eligibility.
- Extend tracing hooks to emit a standardized 'operational_context' tag (workflow, cache-warm-id, rollout-id, invoker-type).
- Add a metrics/log pipeline enrichment stage that attaches the operational_context to spans/metrics before SLO evaluation.
- Implement an attenuation policy layer: if confidence < 0.6, convert burn-rate-triggered pager to Slack-only alert and attach runbook hints; if confidence >= 0.6, escalate to phone page.
- Add anomaly detection integration: gatekeeper will call the anomaly scorer (existing service) to suppress transient spikes with low anomaly persistence.

Non-goals:
- Full rewrite of SLO definitions or escalation policies across all teams (we'll operate per-service opt-in during rollout).
- Replacing existing tracing libraries; we'll add a small shim and example integrations.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Centralized gatekeeper vs. distributed: We chose a centralized gatekeeper to ensure consistent attenuation logic and simpler rollout. Risk is single-point-of-failure; mitigations include caching, graceful fallback, and running gatekeeper in multiple regions.
- Confidence scoring: use a weighted heuristic combining span-level tags (30%), metric anomaly score (40%), and historical SLO trend (30%) to keep the model simple and auditable.
- Latency: gatekeeper must respond within 150ms to avoid alerting path adds significant delay. We'll implement an async enrichment path where possible and synchronous only for final paging decisions.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Instrumentation: add operational_context shim to tracing SDK and 3 example services (router, kv-cache-manager, inference-proxy). (ENG-880315)
2) Pipeline enrichment: add enrichment transform in metrics/log ingestion (vector/agent) to attach operational_context into metrics/spans. (ENG-880316)
3) Gatekeeper service: implement REST endpoint for evaluate_page(payload) and internal library to compute confidence and suggested action. (ENG-880317)
4) Alerting integration: update burn-rate alert templates to invoke gatekeeper via webhook before paging threshold executes. (ENG-880318)
5) Dashboard & QA: add a gated dashboard panel ('Gatekeeper decisions') and synthetic tests to validate suppression vs escalation behavior. (ENG-880319)

Acceptance criteria:
- Gatekeeper returns decision in <=150ms 95th percentile under production-like load.
- False-positive pages reduced by >=30% across pilot services over a 2-week window.
- MTTA for pilot services improved by >=20% for true incidents (measured by post-incident labeling).
- Tracing shim adopted and live in 3 pilot services with operational_context present on >=95% of spans.
- Playbooks updated and SRE/Oncall training completed for attenuation behaviors.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: Deploy gatekeeper to staging, validate latency and decisions with recording traffic.
- Week 1: Enable instrumentation for pilot services (router, kv-cache-manager).
- Week 2: Enable pipeline enrichment and gatekeeper webhook for burn-rate alerts in dry-run (no paging, only log decisions).
- Week 3: Flip attenuation policy for pilot group to Slack-only for low confidence decisions.
- Week 4: Full escalation enabled for high-confidence decisions; monitor for regressions and rollback if false-positive rate rises.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for confidence scoring and policy logic.
- Integration tests with synthetic spans and metric spikes asserting expected decision.
- Load test gatekeeper endpoint to validate latency SLO.
- Post-deploy chaos test: simulate partial pipeline delays to confirm graceful fallback.

Observability & Metrics to track:
- Gatekeeper latency p50/p95/p99.
- Decision distribution: proportion suppressed/slack-only/phone-page.
- False-positive page rate and MTTA for pilot services.
- % of spans with operational_context attached.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Gatekeeper misclassifies real incidents as low confidence -> mitigation: initial policy favors Slack-only not silence, include explicit runbook link and manual escalation button.
- Risk: Added latency to alerting -> mitigation: strict latency budget, multi-region instances, and fast-path bypass for critical SLI breaches above fatal thresholds.
- Risk: Instrumentation rollout gaps -> mitigation: health checks that report % of spans with tags and nightly alerts if coverage drops.

Open questions:
- Should the anomaly scorer be rate-limited per-service? (ops/infra input)
- Should we expose an override API for trusted services to bypass attenuation in emergencies?
- How to version gatekeeper decisions for auditability? (store decisions in events log)

Deliverables:
- Gatekeeper service (Go) + helm chart.
- Tracing shim and example integrations.
- Metrics pipeline enrichment transform and config.
- Updated burn-rate alert templates and dashboards.
- Post-deploy runbook and oncall training doc.
comments: 2025-10-13 - Priya Raman: Initial design review: like the confidence-weighted approach. Suggest adding a feature flag to opt pilot services in/out. Also asked to tie decision logs into audit log retention (compliance).

2025-10-20 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented prototype gatekeeper scoring module and pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gatekeeper/pull/12. Need review for the scoring weights and latency micro-optimizations.

2025-10-25 - SRE Lead (Luca Moretti): Load-tested gatekeeper in staging to 200 QPS; p95=120ms. Recommend in-process cache for recent decisions to shave p95 to target. Also flagged potential region failover behavior.

2025-10-29 - Security (Naomi Ellis): Requested threat model and dataflow diagram. Noted that operational_context may include rollout IDs which could be sensitive in some enterprise deployments. Marked security_review_required=true and requested KMS usage for logs where PII may be present.
2025-11-01 - Aisha Kaur: Updated scope to include runbook link and explicit manual escalation button in Slack flow. Added ENG-880320 as follow-up for audit event storage config.
